query: How far is the Moon from Earth on average, in kilometres?
answer: On average the Moon is about 384,400 km (roughly 238,900 miles) from Earth, measured centre to centre. That is the mean semi-major axis of its orbit, about 384,402 km [1][2]. The orbit is elliptical, so the actual distance changes over each month. At its closest point (perigee) the Moon is around 363,300 km away, and at its farthest (apogee) around 405,500 km [1]. If you average the distance over time instead, you get a slightly larger figure of about 385,000 km. That's why some references give 385,000 km [1].
